purpose: Validate the caller of each IPC queue enqueue and narrow the post-VIDimming stall without changing guest behavior.

instrumentation.change: The [ipc-queue-trace] field previously read r1+132, outside the current frame. It now reads r1+36, where func_8050441C saves its incoming LR after allocating 32 bytes, and labels it caller_lr.
instrumentation.source_function_prologue: func_8050441C stores ctx->lr at current r1+36 after r1 -= 32.

runtime.queue_observation: The request at head 27/tail 28 submits IOS command 6. After that completion, command 7 is observed with head 28/tail 29 and no new IOS packet; the /dev/usb open and three command 7 enqueues follow while outstanding remains zero and head remains 28. No later IOS packet or handler trace appears before the harness stops the live process.

interpretation: The former caller values were invalid stack reads and are discarded. The saved LR now confirms that the final enqueues originate in func_80504780 and func_80505384. The trace narrows the next investigation to guest queue/thread wake and reschedule behavior after completion of command 6; it does not prove which scheduler transition is missing or justify synthetic IOS replies.
next: Trace the queue wake path through func_804E77A4/func_804E6BD4 and guest thread state around the command-6 completion. Verify whether a runnable IOS worker exists and why the guest scheduler does not submit the next ring entry. Do not fake completion or force a device response.
